Notes for [Workshop 2](https://mb5370.bioinformatics.guide/workshop2.html). Run the commands for this workshop in the Terminal, from inside the folder named under each heading. Copy each command you run into a bash chunk.

## Redbean assembly

Commands run in `redbean/`.

```{r}
# cat /pvol/data/amtp4/*_[012].fastq > amtp4.fastq <- using cat to link and join two fasta files 

# running the assembly - wtdbg2 -x ont -g 5m -t 4 -i amtp4.fastq -fo amtp4 wtpoa-cns -t 4 -i amtp4.ctg.lay.gz -fo amtp4.ctg.fa - which uses the data for the initial assembly, this assembly took a few seconds 

# assembly-stats amtp4.ctg.fa - inspecting assembly statistics 
#the closer to the value 0, the more better the contiguity 
#looking at the estimated completeness with the N# /sum 
# 48075(N50)/3816930(sum) = 1.26% 
# 33615(N60)/3816930(sum) = 0.88%
# 28879(N70)/3816930(sum) = 0.76%
# 21464(N80)/3816930(sum) = 0.56%
# 13021(N90)/3816930(sum) = 0.34%
# 2697(M100)/3816930(sum) = 0.07%

#cat /pvol/data/amtp4/*.fastq > amtp4_20x.fastq
#wtdbg2 -x ont -g 5m -t 4 -i amtp4_20x.fastq -fo amtp4_20x
#wtpoa-cns -t 4 -i amtp4_20x.ctg.lay.gz -fo amtp4_20x.ctg.fa - running an assemblege that is 20x the coverage 
# this assemblage for this one took far far longer (146 secs)

#assembly-stats amtp4_20x.ctg.fa - looking at the stats 
#for the first assembleged - n50 took n=23 (23 conguints) to cover 50% of the DNA sequence vs the 2nd assembledge took only 2 conguints to cover 50% of the DNA sequence 


#Stats 

#Flye Assembly 


#bandage 
# sequence more than the base pairs of the genome 
## typically nowhere near enough to assemble a genome - need to know those reads are randomely generated throughout the sequence and make sure there is proper overlap - need 50 to 100x coverage - sequencing 50 to 100x times 
### little piece with 30x depth(coverage) with longer pieces that have 6-7x depth, it is a repeat - all the conguits are passing through it - everytime it gets to assembly - the repeats all look the same (doesnt know how to connect pieces together because there is a repeating spot) - those repeats could be anywhere from the in the genome - puts certain bigger pieces together and says it has an edge that all connect to a repeat at some point 

#coverage depth does not care about overlap - just how much of the genome being covered 
#coverage extent does care about overlap - increases at a lower rate than depth if there is a lot of overlap 

```
